content.subject: English Language Arts
content.framework: Ohio's Learning Standards for English Language Arts (2017)
content.standardText:
Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.
a. Print all upper- and lowercase letters.
b. Use common, proper, and possessive nouns.
c. Use singular and plural nouns with matching verbs in basic sentences (e.g., He hops; We hop).
d. Use personal, possessive, and indefinite pronouns (e.g., I, me, my; they, them, their; anyone, everything).
e. Use verbs to convey a sense of past, present, and future (e.g., Yesterday I walked home; Today I walk home; Tomorrow I will walk home).
f. Use frequently occurring adjectives.
g. Use frequently occurring coordinating and subordinating conjunctions (e.g., and, but, or, so, because).
h. Use determiners (e.g., articles, demonstratives).
i. Use frequently occurring prepositions (e.g., during, beyond, toward).
j. Produce and expand complete simple and compound declarative, interrogative, imperative, and exclamatory sentences in response to prompts.
assessmentTargets: Print all upper- and lowercase letters
Use common, proper, and possessive nouns correctly
Match singular and plural nouns with verbs
Use personal, possessive, and indefinite pronouns
Use verbs to convey past, present, and future
Use frequently occurring adjectives
Use coordinating and subordinating conjunctions
Use determiners correctly
Produce simple and compound sentences of various types

Select an appropriate computation strategy for a specific problem

content.standardText: Two plane or solid figures are congruent if one can be obtained from the other by rigid motion (a sequence of rotations, reflections, and translations).

Explain congruence in terms of rigid motions

records.subject: Mathematics

content.standardText: A strategy for finding the number of objects in a group without having to count every member of the group. For example, if a stack of books is known to have 8 books and 3 more books are added to the top, it is not necessary to count the stack all over again. One can find the total by counting on—pointing to the top book and saying "eight," following this with "nine, ten, eleven. There are eleven books now."
assessmentTargets: Use the counting on strategy to find a total
Explain how counting on differs from counting all

Identify the center and scale factor of a dilation

assessmentTargets: Write a multi-digit number in expanded form
Convert expanded form to standard form

Explain expected value as a weighted average

content.standardText: For a data set with median M, the first quartile is the median of the data values less than M. Example: For the data set {1, 3, 6, 7, 10, 12, 14, 15, 22, 120}, the first quartile is 6. See also: median, third quartile, interquartile range.
assessmentTargets: Determine the first quartile of a data set
Explain the relationship between the first quartile and the median

Explain that fluency does not imply timed tests

Identify the constraints on a and b in the definition of fraction

Calculate probabilities in an independently combined probability model

Identify integers from a set of numbers

content.standardText: A measure of variation in a set of numerical data, the interquartile range is the distance between the first and third quartiles of the data set. Example: For the data set {1, 3, 6, 7, 10, 12, 14, 15, 22, 120}, the interquartile range is 15 − 6 = 9. See also: first quartile, third quartile.
assessmentTargets: Calculate the interquartile range of a data set
Explain interquartile range as a measure of variation

Interpret a line plot to describe a data distribution

The median of a list of values is the value appearing at the center of a sorted version of the list—or the mean of the two central values, if the list contains an even number of values. Example: For the data set {2, 3, 6, 7, 10, 12, 14, 15, 22, 90}, the median is 11.
assessmentTargets: Calculate the median of a data set
Explain how the median is determined for data sets with an even or odd number of values

assessmentTargets: Identify multiplicative inverses of given numbers

Compute the third quartile of a data set

Apply the transitivity principle to compare lengths

(exclusive definition) Districts may choose either definition to use for instruction. Ohio's State Tests' items will be written so that either definition will be acceptable.
assessmentTargets: Identify the inclusive and exclusive definitions of trapezoid
Recognize that either definition is acceptable on Ohio's State Tests
